findings.evidence: TOOLS-items.md section 1: 'Only items with `status: ready` are printed'. Tasks, speak items and cards were still status candidate; the deep file links to 3-do.md twice.
findings.resolution: Items set to ready after a clean item lint (see claims-07); sync 06 now prints both tasks in 3-do.md and both prompts in 4-say.md.

findings.quote: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) rotates the **key material** of a key.
findings.evidence: 'key material' is bolded but no sentence says what it is; the rotation section depends on it.
findings.resolution: Deep rotation step 2 now: 'New requests use new **key material**, the value inside the key that encrypts.' The glossary entry (data/terms.json key-material) carries the full meaning. The fast file is at its word limit, so no second gloss there.

findings.section: IAM policies and other accounts count only when the key policy allows them
findings.quote: A grant allows the use of [exactly one KMS key](../facts/kms.md#kms-grant-allow-only-one-key-temporary).
findings.evidence: Fact kms-grant-allow-only-one-key-temporary: grants are often used for temporary permissions.
findings.resolution: Now: 'A grant, often temporary, allows the use of [exactly one KMS key].'

findings.section: Numbers that decide answers (A-list) and the rotation table
findings.quote: | Custom automatic rotation period | A shorter period needs on-demand rotation |
findings.evidence: On-demand rotation is named but never explained in the prose.
findings.resolution: No room for a new sentence under the L201 limit. On-demand rotation now appears in the rotation table (imported key material row) and the numbers row (capped at 25 times per key), and task kms-t02 step 6, now printed in 3-do.md, explains it in words ('rotate the key material now, on demand ... does not change the automatic rotation schedule').

findings.section: A disabled KMS key can be re-enabled but a deleted one cannot be recovered
findings.quote: For data keys that are already decrypted, the effect is [delayed until the KMS key is used again](../facts/kms.md#kms-unusable-key-data-keys-delayed-effect).
findings.evidence: The sentence states the effect without the cause; 'the effect' has no clear subject.
findings.resolution: Now: 'A service that already holds a plaintext data key keeps using it: the effect is [delayed until the KMS key is used again].'

findings.section: The key type decides who controls the key policy and who sees its use
findings.quote: Why three types? An AWS owned key is a good choice unless you are [required to audit or control the encryption key](../facts/kms.md#kms-aws-owned-key-good-choice-unless-audit).
findings.evidence: The question is answered only for the AWS owned key; the ladder no audit, audit, audit plus control is missing.
findings.resolution: Now: 'Why three types? An AWS owned key fits unless you are [required to audit or control the encryption key]. An AWS managed key adds the audit, and a customer managed key adds control.' The fast deciding question carries the same ladder (exam-006).

findings.section: IAM policies and other accounts count only when the key policy allows them
findings.quote: Why is the key policy the gate? The key owner decides. Even key administrators [do not have permissions to use](../facts/kms.md#kms-key-administrators-cannot-use-key) the key.
findings.evidence: Fact kms-key-administrators-cannot-use-key: administrators can change the key policy and create grants.
findings.resolution: Same fix as claims-15: the cause is now 'the primary way to control access', and the administrators clause says they can change the key policy and create grants for themselves.

findings.section: IAM policies and other accounts count only when the key policy allows them (table and Default row)
findings.evidence: Fact kms-account-principal-delegates-to-iam: the account principal statement lets the account delegate with IAM policies.
findings.resolution: Step 3 now says: 'The default key policy names the account, which lets the account [use IAM policies to delegate the permissions].' The verdict table was cut to fit the word limit (claims-26).

findings.section: IAM policies and other accounts count only when the key policy allows them (last Stop and answer)
findings.quote: A role in account B calls Decrypt on a key in account A. The key policy allows account B. The role's IAM policy has no KMS statement. Does the call succeed?
findings.evidence: The table above answered it row for row.
findings.resolution: Stop and answer now asks about a case the gist misses: 'A key policy in account A names a role of account B. The role's IAM policy has no KMS statement. Can the role decrypt?' (No: cross-account use also needs an IAM policy in the external account.) The table is gone.

findings.quote: **Check 2.** A team turns on automatic rotation. Must its applications change the key ID?
findings.evidence: The Signals table gave the answer to a skimmer.
findings.resolution: Check 2 now: 'A symmetric key has imported key material. Can it rotate automatically?' Answer: No; AWS KMS supports [rotation for imported keys using on-demand rotation]. No signals row states this case.

findings.section: The key type decides who controls the key policy and who sees its use (Before figure caption)
findings.quote: **Figure.** Before: every data store uses a key that AWS manages, and the bank's recordings share it with other customers.
findings.evidence: Read at a glance it says a key AWS manages is shared with other AWS customers.
findings.resolution: Caption and the kms-before spec claim now: 'Before: every store uses a key that AWS manages, and the bank's recordings share a key with the recordings of Callvale's other customers.' Diagram rebuilt. The key type is not named because the story's 'keys that AWS manages' includes SSE-S3 keys, which are not aws/s3 (claims-04).

findings.section: A KMS key protects a data key and the data key encrypts your data
findings.quote: The application sends the encrypted data key back. It is [decrypted by only users with permissions](../facts/kms.md#kms-faq-exported-data-key-encrypted-under-kms-key) for that KMS key.
findings.evidence: Word order reads as broken English; 'It' has two referents.
findings.resolution: Now: 'The encrypted data key goes back to AWS KMS and is [decrypted by only users with permissions] for that KMS key.' One subject, no 'It'. The link text stays the fact's verbatim display (RULINGS 2026-10-11: number-free displays are verbatim phrases).

findings.section: The key type decides who controls the key policy and who sees its use (Stop and answer)
findings.quote: No. RDS does not share a snapshot [encrypted using the AWS managed key](../facts/kms.md#kms-rds-aws-managed-key-snapshot-no-share).
findings.resolution: Answer adds: 'You [cannot change any properties of AWS managed keys], such as the key policy.'

findings.section: A KMS key stays in its Region unless you create a multi-Region key
findings.quote: At stage 4 the bank needs a copy of the data in a second Region, and a key there that can decrypt it.
findings.resolution: Now: 'Later, the bank's contract needs the data, and a key that decrypts it, in a second Region.'
